item.title: Could Artificial Blood Vessels Replace Traditional Bypass Grafts?
item.description: Tissue engineering may soon offer lab-grown blood vessels that function like natural arteries—potentially transforming coronary bypass surgery and vascular medicine.

item.title: Can You Actually Increase Facial Bone Mass After Puberty?
item.description: A scientific analysis of craniofacial growth, endocrine physiology, and what research shows about skeletal change after epiphyseal fusion.

item.title: Chronotherapy: Why When You Take Medicine Matters
item.description: Exploring the emerging field of circadian medicine—how the timing of medications can dramatically affect their efficacy and side effects.

item.title: Cold Exposure and Immunity: What Does the Science Actually Say?
item.description: Separating fact from hype in the cold plunge and cryotherapy craze—what we know, what we don't, and where the research is heading.

item.title: Is Ethics Just Sophisticated Selfishness?

item.title: Experimental Melanoma Vaccine Shows Encouraging Immune Responses
item.description: Researchers are reporting promising immune responses from personalized melanoma vaccines, highlighting a potential breakthrough in cancer immunotherapy.

item.title: The First AI-Designed Vaccine Has Entered Human Trials
item.description: Researchers at Cambridge and DIOSynVax have completed Phase 1 testing of the world's first vaccine whose key protective component was designed entirely by artificial intelligence—a milestone that could reshape pandemic preparedness.

item.title: The Future of Medical Innovation

item.title: The Gut-Brain Axis: Your Microbiome's Role in Mental Health
